name: What is the biggest hidden cost in a second-story addition?

mainEntity.name: Which expenses surprise homeowners most often when they start a second-story addition in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Which expenses surprise homeowners most often when they start a second-story addition in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common hidden costs in a second-story addition are structural and logistical rather than cosmetic. Homeowners are often surprised by foundation reinforcement, framing upgrades, roof reconstruction, stair redesign, utility upsizing, temporary housing, storage, and permit-related revisions. Older homes can reveal hidden damage or outdated systems once walls and ceilings are opened, which can increase the budget quickly. Another common surprise is that the initial design may need revisions after plan check comments or neighborhood review, adding both time and professional fees. Because a second-story addition is a major structural project, a contingency is essential. Homeowners should not judge a bid only by the base construction number. The more helpful question is what is included, what is excluded, and how change orders will be handled if hidden conditions appear after demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest hidden costs are often structural reinforcement, utility upgrades, temporary living expenses, plan revisions, and change orders caused by conditions uncovered during construction. Older homes and properties with special review requirements are especially likely to exceed the initial estimate.
